nodes.title: Level-one algebraic cuspidal spectrum
nodes.statement: Π_alg is the disjoint union over m≥1 of isomorphism classes of irreducible unitary cuspidal representations of PGL_m(A_Q) unramified at every finite prime, whose real Weil parameter is a direct sum of z↦z^p z̄^q with p,q∈½ℤ and p−q∈ℤ and whose restriction to positive real scalars is trivial. Use the paper’s unitary algebraicity convention: the exponents of a summand are (w/2,−w/2), and the action of −1 is scalar. Write rank(π)=m and sd(π)=1 exactly when π≃π∨. The m=1 trivial representation is included. This is a predicate and quotient specialization of AF, not a second definition of automorphic representation.
proofSteps: Specialize the adelic cuspidal space and restricted tensor product at Q, trivial central character and spherical finite components.
Translate algebraicity through the unitary real LLC; keep the scalar −1 condition explicit rather than identifying it with unshifted C-algebraicity.
acceptance: Prove equivalence of the adelic and classical level-one descriptions.
Expose π∨ and the native finite Satake class c_p(π) without choosing eigenvalue order.

nodes.title: Symmetric weight vectors and classical regularity
nodes.statement: W_m consists of decreasing vectors w∈(½ℤ)^m with w_i−w_j∈ℤ and w_i=−w_{m+1−i}. It is regular when, for every i<j, either w_i≠w_j or m≡0 mod4 and (i,j)=(m/2,m/2+1) with w_i=w_j=0. The exceptional double zero is the type-D regularity convention. For regular effective determinant-one parameters satisfying the scalar −1 condition, the vector of weights determines the parameter uniquely. Regularity is essential: the nonregular parameters 3·1 and 1+2e both have determinant one and three zero weights.
proofSteps: Implement half-integral weights using doubled integral coordinates.
Recover multiplicities of I_w from nonzero weights. In the regular domain zero has multiplicity at most two, so dimension and determinant determine its 1/e multiplicities.
acceptance: The regularity predicate must quantify over ordered indices i<j.
The parameter reconstruction theorem must state regularity, determinant and scalar parity; it cannot reconstruct a general nonregular parameter from its weights.
